'''Alanic''' (also known as '''Alanian''', '''Old Ossetic''' and '''Old Ossetian''')<ref name="Multitree"/> is an extinct [[Iranian language]] spoken by the [[Alans]] from about the 1st to the 13th centuries AD,<ref name="Dodykhudoeva">{{cite web |author=Leila Dodykhudoeva |publisher=[[Academia.edu]] |title=The socio-linguistic situation and state of research of the Ossetic language |work=aber.ac.uk |url=https://www.academia.edu/2471710 |access-date=20 January 2025}}</ref> a [[dialect]] directly descended from the earlier [[Scythian languages|Scytho-Sarmatian languages]], which would in turn give rise to the [[Ossetian language]]. [[Byzantine Greek]] authors recorded only a few fragments of this language.<ref>Ladislav Zgusta, "The old Ossetian Inscription from the River Zelenčuk" (Veröffentlichungen der Iranischen Kommission = Sitzungsberichte der österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften. Philosophisch-historische Klasse 486) Wien: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, 1987. {{ISBN|3-7001-0994-6}}{{pb}}Cited in {{cite journal |last1 =Kim |first1 =Ronald |title =On the Historical Phonology of Ossetic: The Origin of the Oblique Case Suffix |journal =Journal of the American Oriental Society |date =2003 |volume =123 |issue =1 |pages =43–72 [54] |doi =10.2307/3217844 |jstor =3217844 }}</ref> The Alans who moved westward in the [[Migration Period]] brought their language to [[Iberia]] and to the [[Maghreb]]<ref>
{{cite book
 |last1                = Wellman
 |first1               = David Joseph
 |date                 = 6 May 2004
 |chapter              = The Foundations of the Eco-Historical Landscape of Moroccan-Spanish Relations
 |title                = Sustainable Diplomacy: Ecology, Religion and Ethics in Muslim-Christian Relations
 |url                  = https://books.google.com/books?id=OTHIAAAAQBAJ
 |series               = Culture and Religion in International Relations
 |publication-place    = New York
 |publisher            = Springer
 |page                 = 56
 |isbn                 = 9781403980977
 |access-date          = 14 July 2025
 |quote                = After more than five centuries of Roman rule, Iberia and the coastal territories of the Maghreb came under the control of competing branches of the ''Vandals'' in the fall of 409; finding the  ''[[Suebi|Seubi]]'' {{sic}} in the northwest or Galicia, the ''[[Silingi|Silings]]'' in the south in Baetica, and the ''Alans'' on the northern coast of the Maghreb.
}}
</ref>
in 409 AD, before being displaced by the invading [[Visigoths]]<ref name="Multitree">{{cite web |title=Alanic |url-status=dead |archive-date=3 May 2021 |publisher=[[Linguist List |LINGUIST List]]|access-date=9 December 2024 |url=http://multitree.org/codes/xln|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210503102259/http://multitree.org/codes/xln |quote=The extinct unknown language of the Alans, who came from Asia and overran the Iberian Peninsula around AD 409, before being displaced by the Visigoths.}}</ref> and by the [[Byzantine Empire]].

Unlike [[Pontic Scythian language|Pontic Scythian]], Ossetian did not experience the evolution of the Proto-Scythian sound /d/ to /ð/ and then /l/, although the sound /d/ did evolve into /ð/ at the beginning of Ossetian words.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Ivantchik |first=Askold I. |author-link=Askold Ivantchik |title=Une légende sur l'origine des Scythes (HDT. IV 5–7) et le problème des sources du ''Scythicos logos'' d'Hérodote |trans-title=A Legend on the Origin of the Scythians (Hdt. IV 5–7) and the problems of the sources of Herodotus's ''Scythicos logo''s |journal=Revue des Études Grecques |trans-work=Review of Greek Studies |volume=112 |issue=1 |date=1999 |jstor=44260011 |pages=156–158 |doi=10.3406/reg.1999.4355 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/44260011 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

According to [[Magomet Isayev]], the Zelenchuk inscription and other historical data give reason to assume that in the 10th–13th centuries, the Alans already had their own unique written language based on the [[Greek alphabet]]. However, subsequent historical events resulted in this written tradition being lost.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ironau.ru/miller-et.html |title=Всеволод Фёдорович Миллер |access-date=2025-02-07 |archive-date=2011-09-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110912084928/http://ironau.ru/miller-et.html |url-status=dead |language=Russian}}</ref> [[William of Rubruck]], who met the Alans in the 13th century, mentioned that they had Greek writing.<ref>Guill. de Rubruc 11, 1—3 (изд. Wyngaert 1929:191—192)</ref>

After the [[Mongol invasions and conquests|Mongols]] destroyed [[Alania|the Alan state]] in the northern Caucasus in 1240, some Alans retreated to the mountains of the [[Caucasus]] and mixed with the indigenous population, becoming the modern-day [[Ossetians]] and their language developing into the Ossetian language.<ref>{{cite book |title=Jazyki mira: Iranskije jazyki. III. Vostotšnoiranskije jazyki |publisher=Indrik |date=1999|pages=105–106|isbn=5-85759-107-4}}</ref>

== Phonology ==
With regard to historical phonology, the archaic [[Digor Ossetian|Digor dialect]] of Ossetian is closest to Alanic.{{cn|date=July 2025}} The main differences are:

* In Alanic the transition ''a'' > ''o'' before nasals has not occurred (''ban'' {{gloss|day}}, ''nam'' {{gloss|name}}).
* Alanic lacked the [[ejective consonant]]s ''pʼ'', ''tʼ'', ''tsʼ'', ''chʼ'', ''kʼ'' and ''kʷʼ'', which were adopted by Ossetian from the Caucasian substrate, as well as ''kh'' (''q''), which was adopted from [[Turkic languages|Turkic]].

==Phrases==
Well-known evidence of the Alanic language are the Alanic phrases in the Theogony of the [[Byzantine Greeks|Byzantine]] author [[John Tzetzes]].

In 1927, the [[Hungarians|Hungarian]] [[Byzantinism|Byzantinist]] I. Moravcsik discovered the full text of the epilogue to the Theogony in the 15th-century Barberinus manuscript in the [[Vatican Library]]. He published the work in 1930, which contained greeting formulas written in the Greek alphabet for the various languages that the [[Byzantine Empire]] had come into contact with in the 12th century. These languages included "Scythian" (in fact, the [[Cuman language]]), "[[Persian language|Persian]]" (in fact, [[Oghuz languages|Turkish-Seljuk]]), [[Latin]], [[Arabic]], [[Russian language|Russian]], [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] and Alanic. Thus, this is the only written monument of Alanic whose ethnolinguistic affiliation has been attested by the person who wrote it.

The translation from [[Greek language|Greek]] and Latin transliterations of greeting phrases in “barbarian” languages was published by S. M. Perevalov in 1998:

τοις Άλανοις προσφθέγγομαι κατά' την τούτων γλώσσαν
: [I address the Alans in their language:]
καλή' ήμερα σου, αυ'θέτα μου, αρχόντισσα, πόθεν είσαι;
: ["Good day, my lord, Archontissa, where are you from?"]
ταπαγχας μέσφιλι χσινά κορθι καντά, και ταλλα.
: [Tapankhas mesfili khsina korthi kanda and so on]
αν δ'εχη Άλάνισσα παπαν φίλον, α'κουσαις ταύτα.
: [If an Alan has a (holy) father as her lover, you will hear this:]
Ουκ αίσχύνεσαι, αυθέντριά μου, να' γαμη το μουνίν σου παπάς
: ["Aren't you ashamed, my lady? After all, your father has relations with you"]
То φάρνετζ κίντζι μέσφιλι καιτζ φουα σαουγγε.
: [Το 'farnetz kintzi mesfili kaitzfua saunge.']

The language of these phrases is an archaic version of the Ossetian language. Thus, ''Tapankhas'' ({{gloss|good day}}) corresponds to Iron ''dæ bon xorz'', Digor ''dæ bon xwarz'' {{gloss|let your day be good}}. A similar phrase, ''daban horz'', was found in the [[Jassic dialect|Jassic]] glossary of 1422.

Both phrases can be compared in their entirety with modern Ossetian analogues:

The first phrase, ''Tapankhas mesfili khsina korthi kanda'', corresponds to the modern Ossetian (Digor):
:: Dæ bon xwarz, me ’fsijni ’xsijnæ. Kurdigæj dæ?
::: "Good afternoon, my master's mistress (wife). Where are you from?"

The second phrase, ''Farnetz kintzi mesfili kaitzfua saunge'', corresponds to the Ossetian
: ’F(s)arm neci (’j) kindzi ’fsijni, kæci fæwwa sawgini.
:: — "There is no shame (for) a lady-daughter-in-law who is a priest's (given to a priest)".<ref name="Kambolov">{{Cite conference|first=Tamerlan|last=Kambolov|title=Some New Observations on the Zelenchuk Inscription and Tzetzes' Alanic Phrases|book-title=Scythians, Sarmatians, Alans — Iranian-Speaking Nomads of the Eurasian Steppes (7-10 May 2007): Abstracts|pages=21–22|location=Barcelona|year=2007|url=http://seneca.uab.es/antiguitat/SCYTHIANS/CONGRESS%20Files/Abstracts%20Barcelona.pdf|access-date=2025-02-05|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080911024632/http://seneca.uab.es/antiguitat/scythians/congress%20files/abstracts%20barcelona.pdf|archivedate=2008-09-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://seneca.uab.es/antiguitat/SCYTHIANS/CONGRESS%20Files/Abstracts%20Barcelona.pdf|title=Источник|access-date=2025-02-05|archive-date=2008-09-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080911024632/http://seneca.uab.es/antiguitat/SCYTHIANS/CONGRESS%20Files/Abstracts%20Barcelona.pdf|url-status=unfit}}</ref>

There has also been a comparison of the word for horse in various Indo-Iranian languages and the reconstructed Alanic word for horse:<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9fdjAAAAMAAJ|title=Studia iranica et alanica|last1=Abaev|first1=Vasiliĭ Ivanovich|last2=l'Oriente|first2=Istituto italiano per l'Africa e|date=1998|publisher=Istituto italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente|language=ru}}{{page needed|date=August 2022}}</ref>

==Zelenchuk inscription==
The Zelenchuk inscription is a 10th-century inscription on a gravestone discovered by archaeologist [[Dmitry Strukov]] in 1888 on the right bank of the [[Bolshoy Zelenchuk|Bolshoy Zelenchuk river]]. It is considered the most famous written monument of the Alanic language or the oldest monument of the [[Ossetian language]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://allingvo.ru/DIGOR/DigoronDialekt.htm|title=ДИГОРСКИЙ ДИАЛЕКТ ОСЕТИНСКОГО ЯЗЫКА|access-date=2025-01-26|archive-date=2010-05-24|language=Russian|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100524060432/http://allingvo.ru/DIGOR/DigoronDialekt.htm}}</ref>

The inscription was read and published in 1893 by Academician [[Vsevolod Miller]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ironau.ru/bse.html|title=Большая советская энциклопедия|access-date=2025-01-26|archive-date=2008-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080621223803/http://ironau.ru/bse.html|language=Russian|url-status=live}}</ref> as follows:

Ις Χς
: [Jesus Christ]
Οατς(?) Νικολαοή
: [Saint (?) Nicholas]
Σαχηρη φουρτ
: [Sakhir's son]
X… ρη φουρτ
: [Χ... and son]
Πακαθαρ Πακαθαη φουρτ
: [Bakatar Bakatai son]
Ανπαλ Αναπαλανη φουρτ
: [Anbal Anabalan son]
λακανη τζηρθε (?)
: [Monument to the Youth (?)]
<λακανητε ηρθε> (?)
: [<Young men Ira (?)>]

According to the modern researcher [[:ru:Камболов, Тамерлан Таймуразович|T. T. Kambolov]], the inscription can be deciphered as follows:

"Jesus Christ, Saint Nicholas, Sakhir son of Khors, Khors son of Bagatar, Bagatar son of Anbalan, Anbalan son of Lag - their graves."

It is assumed that the slab was installed on the site of a collective burial and that names were added as new graves appeared, which can be noticed from the some symbols being drawn differently.<ref name="Зеленчукская надпись">{{cite web|url=http://www.alanica.ru/writing/2.htm|title=Зеленчукская надпись|access-date=2025-02-06|archive-date=2007-11-07|url-status=dead|language=Russian|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071107160435/http://www.alanica.ru/writing/2.htm}}</ref>

In 1892, the inscription was rediscovered by [[:ru:Куликовский, Герман Илларионович|G. I. Kulikovsky]], which he made a new imprint of. This was the last time the monument was seen as expeditions in 1946 and 1964 failed to find the gravestone.<ref name="Зеленчукская надпись"/>
